Q: how to use index find element for android appium A: 
xpath=//android.widget.EditText[2]

The xpath reads "find all android.wdiget.EditText and return the n-th matching node - in your case, the target one is the 2nd in the nodeset; you've mistaken the condition as the n-th chield of the parent node.
Plus, the position in xpath start from 1, not 0.

Q: Test connection failed because of an error in initializing provider A:

First guess, wrong IP or wrong oracle home is being used (and thus different tnsnames.ora). The other guess, I assume the UDL file is being used in a Windows-based PC : the error might be because the COM objects that being used as provider is not installed correctly. Maybe there is a problem with MDAC (Microsoft Data Access Components), you might also need to reinstall Oracle Client with Windows Interfaces enabled in custom options.

Q: user control event handler lost on postback A:

I had a similar issue. It turned out that Akamai was modifying the user-agent string because an setting was being applied that was not needed.

This meant that some .NET controls did not render __doPostBack code properly. This issue has been blogged here.

Q: force number of digits in awk output (no printf) A:

I cannot use printf because each line has a different number and type of fields.

sprintf is more handy there, but you can use printf in this situation. Let file.txt content be

0.000 some stuff
1.000 other different stuff
1.234 even more stuff

then

awk '{printf "%.06f ",$1;for(i=2;i<NF;i+=1){printf "%s ",$i};print $NF}' file.txt

gives output

0.000000 some stuff
1.000000 other different stuff
1.234000 even more stuff

Explanation: I use printf to output 1st field followed by space in desired format, then for-loop with printf and %s specifier, to output all but extreme fields, then print (not printf as I want to output row separator to be appended) to output last field. DISCLAIMER: this solution assume every line inside input data has no less than 2 fields, if this does not hold ignore this answer entirely.

(tested in GNU Awk 5.3.1)

Q: How to improve PaddleOCR performance, it is sometimes not able to detect space in between words A:

PaddleX uses CTC (Connectionist Temporal Classification) decoder, in other words (probability distribution matrix)**

Key finding:** When the space probability is high enough (>0.5), argmax picks SP and the space appears in output. When it's in the 0.3-0.5 range, argmax picks blank instead and the space is lost. The model IS signaling spaces - just not strongly enough for argmax to pick them up in borderline cases.

The best approach I've found that's scalable enough for production cases is to do a fine tuning of both models to optimize space detection and recognition

Follow the following link : https://github.com/PaddlePaddle/PaddleOCR/blob/release/2.6/doc/doc_en/finetune_en.md
